cards.method: HP / Baxter-King / Christiano-Fitzgerald filters
cards.when: a fast trend/cycle decomposition (output gap) without estimating a model; CF-asymmetric fills the end (end-of-sample gap, no missing tail) but is internally full-sample time-varying/revisable — real-time only at the endpoint; a non-revisable real-time gap -> #92 one-sided HP
cards.when_not: you want standard errors or credible bands (-> #58/#59/#60), a common trend across several series (-> #61), or a non-revisable Basel gap (-> #92)

alternatives.criterion: real-time / Basel III credit gap (non-revisable)
avoiding the spurious cycles of the HP filter
you want SE bands + a model-based forecast

output_key_fields: trend: potential output (ts)
cycle: output gap in % of 100*log(GDP) (ts)
lambda: the effective smoothing parameter
na_each_end: how many observations stay blank at each edge (the BK / symmetric-CF endpoint problem)
interpretation_traps: an interior gap silently blanks the WHOLE cycle (silently wrong, so a hard gate)
BK and the symmetric/fixed CF leave nfix observations blank at EACH edge -> the most recent gap is missing
the two-sided HP is revised at the edge (endpoint bias) -> NOT for real-time policy
the choice of lambda (1600 quarterly / Ravn-Uhlig) changes the gap dramatically

CF-asymmetric fills the end BUT the values are revised just as with the two-sided HP: interior points use future data (time-varying weights, Christiano-Fitzgerald 2003) — only the last observation is genuinely one-sided
sources: Hodrick & Prescott 1997 (JMCB)
Baxter & King 1999 (REStat)
Christiano & Fitzgerald 2003 (Int. Econ. Review)
Ravn & Uhlig 2002 (REStat)
Enders 2015

cards.method: Hamilton regression filter
cards.when: an output gap without the spurious dynamics of the HP filter (the Hamilton critique); OLS projection of y_{t+h} on p lags; residual=gap
cards.when_not: you want a smooth potential output, a forecast/state uncertainty (state space), or band-pass isolation (BK/CF)

alternatives.criterion: you accept two-sided smoothing
a real-time Basel gap
a model-based gap with SE

output_key_fields: cycle: output gap (residual y_{t+h}-fitted)
trend: fitted (the predictable component)
n_lost_trend: h+p-1 leading blanks; n_lost_random: h
coefficients/glance (ham_regression): OLS diagnostics (term/estimate/p_value, aic, r_squared)
interpretation_traps: p>=2 is MANDATORY (p=1 does not capture seasonality)
the lag is POSITIONAL, not calendar-aware -> calendar gaps silently desynchronise h and p
the default is h=2*ppy and p=ppy (frequency-aware); Hamilton's published 8/4 is quarterly and is silently wrong for monthly data
leading blanks in trend/cycle are expected (date alignment), not an error
sources: Hamilton 2018 'Why You Should Never Use the Hodrick-Prescott Filter' (REStat 100(5))
Enders 2015

cards.method: Kalman filter/smoother + unobserved-components models
cards.when: linear-Gaussian UC with ML estimation + an exact Kalman filter (real-time) & smoother (two-sided); trend+SSMcycle -> output gap with SE bands
cards.when_not: non-Gaussian data, you want a full Bayesian posterior (-> #60), a common trend across several series (-> #61), or a time-varying exog_handle

alternatives.criterion: an SVD-based Kalman recursion; equivalent, but this card handles diffuse initialisation better
you want credible bands instead of asymptotic SE
a fast filter without estimation

output_key_fields: filtered_states (att): real-time/one-sided
smoothed_states (alphahat): two-sided/historical
trend: potential output; cycle: output gap (+_se bands)
log_lik, variances H/Q, convergence, diffuse_d
interpretation_traps: non-convergence of fitSSM -> silently junk variances (post-gate convergence==0)
diffuse_d: the first d filtered values have ~infinite variance (unreliable)
the filtered gap != the smoothed gap (the real-time gap is revised)
sources: Durbin & Koopman 2012 (State Space Methods, 2nd ed.)
Harvey 1989 (Structural Time Series & Kalman Filter)
Helske 2017 JSS 78(10) (exponential-family state-space models)

cards.method: Dynamic linear models (state space)
cards.when: linear-Gaussian state space with an SVD Kalman filter (numerically stable); trend + a rotation-form stochastic cycle -> output gap
cards.when_not: you want diffuse initialisation or non-Gaussian observations (-> #58), a Gibbs/Bayesian treatment (-> #60), time-varying regression, or a multivariate system (-> #61)

alternatives.criterion: an equivalent UC model; better diffuse handling
a full posterior
no model

output_key_fields: smoothed_states/filtered_states + _se (two-sided vs real-time)
trend (smoothed level), slope, cycle (output gap)
one_step_forecast, log_lik, par, convergence
interpretation_traps: CRITICAL: a free AR(2) cycle -> a DEGENERATE decomposition (level & cycle cancel each other out); the wrapper builds a rotation form at a FIXED frequency
dlmMLE non-convergence -> junk variances (post-gate)
dlmFilter/dlmSmooth carry a time-0 prior row (n+1) -> dropFirst
dlmForecast works on constant models ONLY
sources: West & Harrison 1997 (Bayesian Forecasting & Dynamic Models)
Petris, Petrone & Campagnoli 2009 (Dynamic Linear Models with the reference, Springer UseR!)
Petris 2010 JSS 36(12)

cards.method: Bayesian state space
cards.when: a full posterior + credible bands via MCMC; bsm_lg (level+slope+seasonal) -> a stochastic trend; ar1_lg -> a Bayesian output-gap factor
cards.when_not: you want a fast point estimate (-> #58/#59), non-Gaussian data, plain forecasting, or a multivariate system (-> #61)

alternatives.criterion: an ML point estimate + asymptotic SE, fast
more general Bayesian models

output_key_fields: theta_summary: posterior of the variances/parameters
trend (state level), cycle (state signal ar1_lg), seasonal: {time,mean,sd,lower,upper} credible band
states_summary: per-time records (variable/time/Mean/SD/probs%)
acceptance_rate
interpretation_traps: the seed is MANDATORY: the sampler's own default is random and this engine is deterministic
the MCMC output is a jump chain (the counts are weights) -> read the weighted summary ONLY, never the raw array
a low acceptance_rate -> poor mixing, check it before trusting the bands
sources: Helske & Vihola 2021 (Bayesian inference for non-linear and non-Gaussian state-space models)
Durbin & Koopman 2012

cards.method: Multivariate state space (output gap / NAIRU / DFA)
cards.when: Dynamic Factor Analysis: m common latent trends from n macro indicators; a common labour-market trend = a robust NAIRU proxy; y-fitted = output-gap-style
cards.when_not: a univariate series (-> #58/#59), an explicit structural NAIRU/Phillips model (EXCLUDED: weakly identified), or an automatic-differentiation back end (not exposed)

alternatives.criterion: nowcasting factors
one series
no model

output_key_fields: factors: m x T COMMON smoothed trends (+factors_se, filtered_factors)
loadings: Z n x m factor loadings
gaps: y - fitted (output-gap-style)
log_lik/AIC/AICc, convergence
interpretation_traps: ORIENTATION TRAP (silently wrong #1): a T x n matrix is accepted SILENTLY -> garbage; VARIABLES GO IN ROWS (transpose)
non-convergence (conv=1/2/10=maxit) -> a post-gate blocker
DFA factors: the sign/scale/rotation is undetermined -> interpret loadings+factor together
parametric/innovations CIs = a seeded bootstrap (seed gate)
sources: Holmes, Ward & Wills 2012, multivariate autoregressive state-space models for time-series data
Zuur et al. 2003 (Dynamic factor analysis, Environmetrics)
Harvey 1989

cards.method: One-sided HP filter (Basel III credit gap)
cards.when: a ONE-SIDED (real-time/recursive) HP trend; the OFFICIAL Basel III methodology for the credit-to-GDP gap / CCyB (lambda=400000 quarterly)
cards.when_not: historical analysis where revision is acceptable (the two-sided HP, #56), a band-pass filter (#56), or model-based uncertainty (#58/#59/#60)

alternatives.criterion: the same lambda but revisable
an end-of-sample band-pass (nothing blank at the end); real-time only at the endpoint — internally revisable
a real-time OLS gap

output_key_fields: trend: one-sided HP trend (data_frame)
cycle: x - trend = credit gap / output gap (data_frame -> records)
lambda (400000 for the Basel credit gap), n, series
interpretation_traps: the one-sided trend DIFFERS from the two-sided one at the same lambda -> do not compare them as equals
lambda=400000 is the Basel-mandated value for quarterly credit data (NOT 1600)
an interior gap or infinity silently blanks the trend (hard gate)
lambda<0 runs WITHOUT an error but gives a wrong result (hard gate); lambda=0 blanks almost everything
sources: BCBS 2010 'Guidance for national authorities operating the countercyclical capital buffer' (Basel III)
Drehmann, Borio & Tsatsaronis 2011 (BIS Working Papers, credit-to-GDP gap)
Hodrick & Prescott 1997
Stock & Watson 1999 (one-sided HP)

cards.method: Bayesian time-varying-parameter (TVP) regression with global-local shrinkage (triple/double/ridge) + SV
cards.when: a single equation y ~ x; you suspect the coefficients CHANGE over time (structural change, changing elasticities); you want a full posterior + automatic shrinkage towards a constant coefficient wherever no variation is needed
cards.when_not: constant coefficients suffice (OLS/#46); multivariate joint dynamics (a VAR, cat. 03); a pure trend/cycle decomposition of one series (#56-61 filters/state space); very large samples (MCMC cost)

alternatives.criterion: you want a structural trend/cycle/seasonal decomposition or Kalman filtering, not a TVP regression with shrinkage

alternatives.alt: #46 panel or OLS with constant coefficients
alternatives.criterion: theta_sr ~0 for ALL coefficients — there is no time variation, the constant model suffices
you want TVP without global-local shrinkage (a baseline; it does not shrink towards a constant)
a non-gaussian likelihood or a hierarchical structure beyond TVP+SV

output_key_fields: beta_paths: per covariate, the posterior median + 95% CI of the time-varying coefficient (chart-data, of length n_obs+1: the states t=0.T)
theta_sr_median: sqrt(theta), the state standard deviation per covariate; ~0 => the coefficient is CONSTANT (shrinkage collapsed it), a large value => substantive time variation
beta_mean_median: the constant (mean) level of each coefficient
sigma2_median: the observation variance — a scalar when sv=False, a path of length n_obs when sv=True
shrinkage: a_xi/a_tau (double/triple only)/kappa2_B/lambda2_B — the global shrinkage hyperparameters
stvp_forecast: pred_median/pred_lower/pred_upper per horizon; stvp_lpds: lpds (larger=a better forecast)
interpretation_traps: theta_sr is the sqrt of the variance AND non-centered (it can come out negative in the posterior sample; the ABSOLUTE value/distance from 0 is what matters) — |theta_sr|~0 means a constant coefficient, NOT a zero coefficient (see beta_mean)
beta_paths have n_obs+1 points (the initial state t=0 is included); beta_time runs 0.T
stvp_forecast REQUIRES future values of the regressors; it does not forecast x itself, and the new data must have at least as many rows as the horizon, otherwise it fails
stvp_lpds accepts EXACTLY one hold-out row (it fails otherwise); compare mod_type through the sum of the LPDS over a rolling hold-out
ridge has NO a_xi/a_tau (it performs no shrinkage selection); do not look for the shrinkage fields there
the MCMC is stochastic: the seed is mandatory; a different seed => different (but compatible) posterior summaries
sources: Knaus, Bitto-Nemling, Cadonna & Frühwirth-Schnatter 2021 JSS 100(13) (shrinkage in the time-varying parameter model framework)
Bitto & Frühwirth-Schnatter 2019 (J. Econometrics 210:75, the Normal-Gamma / double shrinkage prior)
Cadonna, Frühwirth-Schnatter & Knaus 2020 (Econometrics 8:20, the triple gamma prior)
Frühwirth-Schnatter & Wagner 2010 (J. Econometrics 154:85, the non-centered parameterization / theta_sr)
precondition_tools: c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the panel/time series as a numeric data_frame)
stvp_lpds (the out-of-sample log predictive density: compare mod_type / TVP vs constant on a hold-out sample)
stvp_forecast (a predictive forecast with future regressor values)

cards.method: Bayesian regression with time-varying (random-walk) coefficients — HMC (Stan)
cards.when: you want a regression whose coefficients EVOLVE over time (structural change / time-varying elasticities / a changing NAIRU slope), gaussian or counts (poisson/binomial), with a full posterior + CI
cards.when_not: constant coefficients (a classic lm/GLM); pure trend-cycle extraction without regressors (#56-61); you need a formal forecast (predict; outside the surface here); a very large n/many covariates (HMC is expensive)

alternatives.criterion: you want a hierarchical/multilevel or non-gaussian GLM WITHOUT a time-varying structure (constant or group-varying coefficients)
a general (non-linear/non-gaussian) state-space model with particle MCMC rather than the HMC-marginalised approach
a purely frequentist state-space trend/level WITHOUT time-varying regression coefficients

output_key_fields: converged / max_rhat / n_divergent (tvreg_fit): the convergence gate (converged=True only when max_rhat<1.1 and there are no divergences)
coef_names / n_time_varying (tvreg_fit): the names of the time-varying coefficients, including the time-varying intercept or level
sigma_summary (tvreg_fit): the posterior of the standard deviations (sigma_y is the observation sd; each sigma_rw is the rate of change of one coefficient)
fitted (tvreg_fit): the posterior mean fitted values — chart data
coef_table (tvreg_coef): long records {beta, time, median, lower, upper, mean, sd} — the time-varying posterior median with a 95% band (chart data)
interpretation_traps: convergence FIRST: when converged=False (max_rhat>=1.1, or any divergence) the estimates are unreliable — raise the iterations or tighten the priors, and do NOT interpret them
a small iter=400 -> low-ESS warnings; it is deliberately SMALL for a node — raise iter for a final analysis
poisson and binomial families put the coefficients on the LINK scale; use tvreg_coef with exponentiate=True for a multiplicative reading
sigma_rw*->0 ⇒ the coefficient is PRACTICALLY constant (negligible time variation); a large sigma_rw ⇒ strong variation
double intercept: the rw term adds its own time-varying level; the wrapper prepends '-1 +' so that only ONE remains (identifiability)
counts, silently wrong: walker_glm accepts non-integer y SILENTLY — the gate blocks it (non-negative integers; binomial requires y<=u)
sources: Helske 2022 (Bayesian generalized linear models with time-varying coefficients)
Vihola, Helske & Franks (2020), Importance sampling type estimators based on approximate marginal MCMC, Scandinavian J. of Statistics 47(4):1339-1376 (the walker_glm exact-approximate weighting)
Durbin & Koopman (2012), Time Series Analysis by State Space Methods 2nd ed. (the random-walk coefficient state-space representation)
precondition_tools: c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading a TIME-ordered data_frame; one row = one time point)
tvreg_fit (max_rhat/n_divergent/converged: check the HMC convergence BEFORE interpreting the coefficients)

cards.method: Particle-filter (bootstrap) log-likelihood + iterated filtering (IF2) MLE for non-linear non-Gaussian state-space models
cards.when: a non-linear / non-Gaussian state-space model where the Kalman filter does not apply; you want a particle-filter log-likelihood (pf_loglik) or a simulation-based MLE (pf_iterated_filtering) on one of the built-in templates gompertz/ricker/ou2
cards.when_not: a linear-Gaussian model (-> #58/#59/#60/#61, the exact Kalman filter); custom dynamics beyond the three templates (that would need compiled user code, blocked for security); a full Bayesian posterior over the parameters (-> #60)

alternatives.criterion: the model is linear-Gaussian -> an exact Kalman filter, not a particle approximation

alternatives.alt: the bootstrap or psi particle filter of #60
alternatives.criterion: you want Bayesian inference (MCMC) with a particle filter rather than a point MLE
a low min_ess (particle depletion) or a non-converging loglik_trace

output_key_fields: loglik: the particle-filter log-likelihood (pf_loglik) or the final IF2 loglik (pf_iterated_filtering); a Monte Carlo estimate, it varies with Np/the seed
eff_sample_size / min_ess (pf_loglik): the ESS per time point; a low min_ess -> particle depletion, raise Np
cond_log_lik (pf_loglik): the conditional log-likelihood per time point (chart-data)
estimates / estimated (pf_iterated_filtering): the final values of ALL the parameters + which names were estimated
loglik_trace / traces (pf_iterated_filtering): the loglik & the parameter path per IF2 iteration — a convergence diagnostic (chart-data)
converged: a finite loglik (& estimates); a stateless-node flag instead of stderr
interpretation_traps: the loglik is a STOCHASTIC Monte Carlo estimate — two runs with a different seed/Np give different values; compare only with the same seed/Np
a low min_ess (e.g. << Np) means particle depletion -> the loglik is unreliable, NOT that the model is bad; raise Np
IF2 (pf_iterated_filtering) has NO hard convergence test — judge convergence from the loglik_trace (it must stabilise) & the converged flag, not from a single run
the initial-value parameters (…_0, e.g. X_0/N_0/x1_0) are NOT perturbed by default; to estimate them pass them explicitly in estimate
SECURITY: ONLY the built-in templates are exposed; there is no way to supply custom C dynamics (the compile/eval surface is blocked)
sources: King, Nguyen & Ionides (2016), Journal of Statistical Software <
Ionides, Nguyen, Atchadé, Stoev & King 2015, 'Inference for dynamic and latent variable models via iterated, perturbed Bayes maps', PNAS 112(3):719 (the IF2 algorithm)
Arulampalam et al. 2002, IEEE Trans. Signal Processing 50(2):174 (the bootstrap particle filter)
precondition_tools: pf_loglik (run the particle filter first: check for a finite loglik & min_ess before IF2)
pf_iterated_filtering (the IF2 MLE; check the converged field & the loglik_trace for convergence)

cards.method: BEAST — a Bayesian decomposition into trend + seasonality + change points with posterior change probabilities
cards.when: you want to decompose a regular series into trend + seasonality AND simultaneously locate structural breaks / change points with PROBABILITIES (a posterior), not a point decision; ideal when the number/location of the breaks is unknown and you want uncertainty per time point
cards.when_not: irregular or unevenly sampled data (the irregular variant is outside this node's scope); a pure output-gap or potential-output estimate (-> #56/#92); one KNOWN break at a known date (-> #3); a state-space model with an explicit unobserved-components structure (-> #58/#59)

alternatives.criterion: you only want a trend/cycle gap without change-point uncertainty
a frequentist multiple-break test with explicit break dates + SC/BIC
an explicit linear-Gaussian state-space UC model (level+slope+seasonal) with smoothing
outside the engine — only a point forecast without posterior break probabilities

output_key_fields: Y and SD in trend: the fitted trend plus the posterior standard deviation per time point (a chart-ready band)
trend.cpOccPr: the per-time posterior change-probability curve (of length n, ∈[0,1]) — the MAIN chart-data
cp / cpPr / cpCI in trend: the change-point positions in decreasing probability, the probability of each, and the credible interval of the position
ncp / ncp_median / ncp_mode in trend: the posterior distribution of the number of change points
Y, cpOccPr and amp in season_component: the seasonal component and the seasonal change probability (absent when season='none')
R2 / RMSE / marg_lik / sig2: goodness of fit + the marginal likelihood + the noise
beast_changepoints: n_cp/cp/cpPr filtered by a threshold (with no NaN padding)
interpretation_traps: ncp is a posterior MEAN (non-integer, e.g. 0.14) — NOT a fixed number of breaks; read ncp_median/ncp_mode + cpPr for a decision
cp is returned with NaN padding at the end (the maximum slots); the wrapper already filters it — do not read the raw slots
a gap in y does not fail — it is INTERPOLATED silently; the wrapper blocks it with a hard gate, for determinism
harmonic/dummy seasonality WITHOUT a period -> BEAST silently guesses the periodicity (non-deterministic); the wrapper requires it explicitly
cpOccPr (the per-time curve) ≠ cpPr (per detected cp): the former is the chart-data, the latter is the probability of the top change points
stochastic MCMC: the same seed ⇒ an identical result; the default seed=2025
sources: Zhao et al. 2019 Remote Sensing of Environment 232 (a Bayesian estimator of abrupt change, seasonality and trend)
Zhao, Wulder et al. 2019, 'Detecting change-point, trend, and seasonality in satellite time series data..', Remote Sensing of Environment 232:111181 (the BEAST algorithm)
live introspection of the trend and season output blocks (cpOccPr/cp/cpPr/cpCI/ncp); reproducibility comes from the MCMC seed
precondition_tools: beast_decompose (the PRODUCER: run it first to obtain the fitted beast handle)
beast_changepoints (the CONSUMER: extracting change-point positions + probabilities with a threshold)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading the series from a file -> num_array)

cards.method: Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Regression (AutoSTR) — trend + multiple/complex seasonality + remainder with CIs per component
cards.when: a univariate seasonal series, possibly with several seasonal periods; you want a trend plus one or more seasonal components with confidence intervals, and/or the seasonally adjusted series; robust to outliers (robust=True)
cards.when_not: a non-seasonal series (frequency<2 -> the trend filters of #56); forecasting (this decomposition does not forecast — use #58-#60, or ARIMA); latent common factors across several series (-> #61); manual custom predictors (that needs the low-level interface, outside this node)

alternatives.criterion: a non-seasonal series — only a trend/cycle decomposition (the output gap)
common latent trends across MANY series, not one
a state-space trend+seasonal model with forecasting/filtering
you do not need CIs — a faster decomposition

output_key_fields: components: a named list of numeric vectors (Data/Trend/Seasonality <period>../Random) — chart-data
component_names: the column order; n_seasonal: the number of seasonal components (>1 for msts)
confidence_intervals: {lower, upper} per predictor component (absent when no confidence level is given)
fitted: {fitted, lower, upper}, the overall fit band (absent when no confidence level is given)
cvMSE: the cross-validated MSE of the lambda selection (blank on the robust path); plus the robust and confidence flags
seasadj (regdec_seasadj): the seasonally adjusted series = the sum of the included components (default Trend+Random)
interpretation_traps: seasadj.STR SILENTLY ignores unknown include names (a warning + skip) -> the node blocks them with a hard gate
the decomposition silently accepts gaps -> the node requires a complete series (a gap gate)
the seasonal component names are 'Seasonality <period>' (e.g. 'Seasonality 12'); msts -> several of them
cvMSE is blank on the robust path, where no cross-validated MSE is produced — do not read it as a perfect fit
STR is a decomposition, NOT a forecast; to forecast, apply state space/ARIMA to the seasadj series
sources: Dokumentov & Hyndman, 'STR: Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Regression', INFORMS J. Data Science 2022
Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice 3rd ed. §3.7 (STL/STR decomposition)
precondition_tools: regdec_decompose (it produces the decomposition object; gaps, non-seasonality and length are hard gates)
regdec_seasadj (the seasonally adjusted series; include must be a subset of the component names)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading the series from a file before building the ts)

cards.method: STL decomposition (seasonal-trend-loess) tolerant of gaps and short series
cards.when: a univariate seasonal series; you want a seasonal/trend/remainder decomposition when there are gaps, or the series is short and does not cover a whole number of periods
cards.when_not: multiple or changing seasonality (-> X-13, #4, or an STL with several seasonal windows); a structural state-space model with uncertainty (-> #58/#59); a pure trend-cycle output gap (-> #56/#92)

alternatives.criterion: no gaps and complete whole periods; then the plain STL suffices
you want only trend/cycle (the output gap), not a seasonal term
an official seasonal adjustment with calendar/outlier regressors

output_key_fields: seasonal/trend/remainder: numeric vectors of length n (raw = seasonal + trend + remainder at the observed points)
raw: the original series, blank at the gaps; weights: the outer-loop robustness weights in [0,1], where a low value marks an outlier
time: the numeric time index; n_obs/n_missing: the number of observations and of gaps
n_p/periodic/s_window/t_window/l_window/s_degree/t_degree: the final parameters that were used
interpretation_traps: an even s_window or t_window is SILENTLY rounded up to the next odd value; the wrapper blocks it with an explicit odd-number gate, so you never believe the value you passed was the one used
s_window='periodic' forces s_degree=0 and an enormous internal span, fixing the seasonality; for an evolving seasonality supply a finite odd s_window
trend and seasonal have NO gaps even when raw does (they are interpolated across the blocks); the remainder stays blank at the original gaps
low weights (~0) mark points that the robust loop down-weighted as outliers, not an error
an s_degree of 1 or 2 requires enough points per subseries; for very short series prefer s_window='periodic'
sources: Cleveland, Cleveland, McRae & Terpenning 1990 (STL), J. Official Statistics 6:3-73
precondition_tools: c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading the series when it is not already a series handle)
stl_tolerant_decompose (the decomposition itself; the robustness weights reveal outliers)

cards.method: Nonparametric detrending & output gap (loess / smoothing spline / Friedman super-smoother)
cards.when: you want a trend/cycle or output gap without a parametric trend form; a smooth, data-driven detrending of a series (loess, a smoothing spline, or the super-smoother); a fast atheoretical benchmark for the gap
cards.when_not: you want economic structure or potential output with shocks (-> #58-#61); a band-pass cycle at a specific frequency (-> #56); a real-time one-sided gap with no end-point revision (-> #92 or #57); very short series (n<4)

alternatives.criterion: you want an HP or band-pass cycle at a defined frequency rather than a free non-parametric trend
you need a real-time (one-sided) gap with no revision of the end points
you want a regression-based filter without the HP spurious-cycle problem
you want a structural unobserved-components/state-space potential output with shocks & credible bands
you want automatic smoothing selection instead of a manual span

output_key_fields: trend: numeric, of the same length as y (the non-parametric trend; chart-data)
cycle: y - trend (np_detrend; the cyclical component / gap in levels)
gap: the output gap by mode (np_output_gap; pct=% deviation, log=100*the log difference, level=y-trend)
smoother: the parameters per method — loess {span, degree, equivalent_df}; the smoothing spline {spar, lambda, df, crit, cv}; the super-smoother {span}
x/y/n: the index, the original series, the number of observations
interpretation_traps: atheoretical: the gap is statistical, NOT economic potential output — do not interpret it as structural

end-point instability: loess and the smoothing spline are two-sided, so the ends of the trend and the gap are revised as new data arrive (exactly as with the HP filter); for real-time work use #92 or #57

a higher smoothing-spline spar gives a less flexible trend, and so a larger gap; a larger span in loess or the super-smoother gives a smoother trend; the smoothing choice determines the amplitude of the gap
mode='pct' requires trend != 0; mode='log' requires y>0 & trend>0 (explicit gates; for rates/growth around 0 use mode='level')
supsmu sorts x internally; the trend is realigned back to the original order (approx) so that cycle = y - trend is correct
sources: Cleveland, Devlin & Grosse 1988 J. Econometrics 37(1) (regression by local fitting); Friedman 1984 (a variable-span smoother)
Cleveland, Grosse & Shyu 1992 (loess, local regression); Friedman 1984 SLAC PUB-3477 (the super smoother)
Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman 2009 ESL §5 (smoothing splines, GCV)
Hamilton 2018 REStat 100:831 (the HP critique -> the motivation for atheoretical benchmarks)
precondition_tools: np_detrend (get the trend+cycle; check that the cycle looks mean-≈0 and stationary)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the series from a file before detrending)

cards.method: Beveridge-Nelson decomposition and the BN filter
cards.when: a model-based trend-cycle split that survives the Hamilton critique and produces a small, plausible output gap
cards.when_not: you want a purely statistical filter with no time-series model; the series is not integrated

alternatives.criterion: you accept its end-point and spurious-cycle problems
a model-based permanent-transitory split

alternatives.alt: BN filter with a fixed persistence prior
alternatives.criterion: the unrestricted BN cycle is implausibly small

output_key_fields: trend, cycle: the permanent and transitory components
delta: the persistence parameter, where the BN filter is used
cycle_amplitude: which is small by construction under BN
model_order: the ARIMA order the decomposition rests on
interpretation_traps: THE BN CYCLE IS SMALL AND NOISY by construction, and many users mistake that for a failure -- it is a property of the permanent-transitory decomposition, not a bug
the decomposition depends entirely on the fitted ARIMA order; different orders give very different trends
the BN trend and cycle are perfectly negatively correlated by construction, which rules out interpreting their comovement
sources: Beveridge & Nelson 1981 (Journal of Monetary Economics 7:151-174)
Kamber, Morley & Wong 2018 (Review of Economics and Statistics 100:550)

cards.method: Unobserved components with stochastic volatility
cards.when: the trend and the volatility of shocks both move over time, as with inflation trend and its changing uncertainty
cards.when_not: the volatility is constant, where a standard unobserved-components model suffices; the sample is too short for the sampler

alternatives.criterion: volatility is stable
both level and volatility move
the coefficients rather than the variances move

output_key_fields: trend: the estimated stochastic trend
volatility: the time-varying shock volatility
credible_bands: posterior bands on both
convergence: sampler diagnostics
interpretation_traps: THE SIGNAL-TO-NOISE RATIO IS WEAKLY IDENTIFIED and the prior does much of the work; report the prior and its sensitivity, not just the posterior
trend estimates at the end of the sample are revised heavily as data arrive -- real-time and final estimates differ substantially
sampler convergence must be checked; a plausible trend from an unconverged chain is still wrong
sources: Stock & Watson 2007 (Journal of Money, Credit and Banking 39:3-33)
Chan 2013 (Journal of Business and Economic Statistics 31:229)
pymc

cards.method: MSTL and robust multiple-seasonality decomposition
cards.when: the series has several seasonal cycles at once -- daily and weekly, or weekly and annual -- which a single-period decomposition cannot separate
cards.when_not: there is one seasonal period; the series is too short to identify the longest cycle

alternatives.criterion: one seasonal period
several seasonal periods
you want the seasonality as regressors

output_key_fields: trend, seasonal, remainder: the components, one seasonal per period
periods: the seasonal periods decomposed
seasonal_strength: strength per period
robust: whether outlier-resistant weights were used
interpretation_traps: THE ORDER OF EXTRACTION MATTERS when periods are not harmonically related; components extracted first absorb variation the later ones then cannot see
a period longer than half the sample cannot be identified and produces a component that is really trend
without robust weighting a few outliers distort the entire seasonal pattern
sources: Bandara, Hyndman & Bergmeir 2021 (International Journal of Operational Research, forthcoming)
Cleveland, Cleveland, McRae & Terpenning 1990 (Journal of Official Statistics 6:3)
statsmodels.tsa.seasonal.MSTL

cards.method: Singular spectrum analysis
cards.when: decomposing a series into trend, oscillations and noise without assuming a parametric model, using the spectrum of its trajectory matrix
cards.when_not: you need a model for forecasting with intervals; the series is too short for the embedding window

alternatives.criterion: the components are seasonal and additive
the oscillations are not at a fixed known period
you want a time-frequency view

output_key_fields: components: the reconstructed components
eigenvalues: the singular spectrum, which shows how many components matter
grouping: which singular triples were grouped into each component
window_length: the embedding window used
interpretation_traps: THE GROUPING OF SINGULAR TRIPLES INTO COMPONENTS IS A JUDGEMENT, not an estimate; different groupings give different trends from identical eigenvalues
the embedding window length determines what can be separated and is bounded by half the sample
components are ordered by variance, not by interpretability; the first is not necessarily the trend
sources: Golyandina, Nekrutkin & Zhigljavsky 2001, Analysis of Time Series Structure: SSA and Related Techniques
Hassani 2007 (Journal of Data Science 5:239)

cards.method: Boosted Hodrick-Prescott filter
cards.when: the ordinary HP filter leaves systematic structure in its cycle, and boosting removes it by refiltering the residual until a stopping rule fires
cards.when_not: you have already rejected HP on principle; the stopping rule cannot be justified for the series

alternatives.criterion: the conventional filter with its known problems
you want HP but with the leftover trend removed
you want to avoid HP entirely

output_key_fields: trend, cycle: the boosted components
n_iterations: boosting rounds, and the stopping rule that ended them
stopping_criterion: the criterion value path
comparison: the plain HP components for reference
interpretation_traps: BOOSTING DOES NOT FIX HP'S END-POINT PROBLEM; the last observations are still revised heavily as data arrive, and boosting can amplify that
the stopping rule determines how much trend is extracted; running to convergence removes almost everything into the trend
lambda still has to be chosen, and the conventional values remain conventions
sources: Phillips & Shi 2021 (International Economic Review 62:521-570)
Hamilton 2018 (Review of Economics and Statistics 100:831)
statsmodels

cards.method: Recursive least squares with CUSUM paths
cards.when: watching coefficients and residuals evolve as the sample grows, to see instability that a full-sample regression averages away
cards.when_not: the sample is too short for recursive estimates to stabilise; you want a formal break test at an unknown date instead

alternatives.criterion: you want to see the coefficient paths
you want a formal stability band
you want a fixed window rather than an expanding one

output_key_fields: recursive_coefficients: the coefficient paths with bands
cusum, cusum_squared: the cumulative sum paths
bounds: the significance bands the paths must stay inside
first_crossing: where a path leaves the band, if it does
interpretation_traps: EARLY RECURSIVE ESTIMATES ARE ESTIMATED ON VERY FEW OBSERVATIONS and swing wildly; the early part of the path is not evidence of instability
CUSUM has low power against a break that does not shift the mean of the residuals; CUSUM-squared complements it by targeting variance shifts
the bands are pointwise in construction and are frequently read as if they were joint
sources: Brown, Durbin & Evans 1975 (JRSS-B 37:149-192)
statsmodels.regression.recursive_ls

cards.method: Unobserved components with correlated trend and cycle innovations
cards.when: the standard assumption that trend and cycle shocks are uncorrelated is not innocuous, and relaxing it changes the estimated gap substantially
cards.when_not: the correlation is not identified in your specification; the sample is too short to estimate it

alternatives.criterion: the conventional restriction
the restriction is relaxed and tested
perfect negative correlation, the opposite extreme

output_key_fields: trend, cycle: the components under the estimated correlation
rho: the trend-cycle innovation correlation
restriction_test: likelihood-ratio test that rho is zero
cycle_amplitude: which changes sharply with rho
interpretation_traps: THE ZERO-CORRELATION RESTRICTION IS WHAT MAKES THE CYCLE LARGE; relaxing it typically produces a much smaller, BN-like cycle, and the difference is the entire substantive debate
rho is weakly identified and the likelihood can be nearly flat in it -- a point estimate without a profile likelihood is not informative
the estimated output gap is not comparable across specifications with different rho
sources: Morley, Nelson & Zivot 2003 (Review of Economics and Statistics 85:235-243)
Watson 1986 (Journal of Monetary Economics 18:49)
statsmodels

cards.method: Ensemble Kalman and square-root filters
cards.when: the state-space model is nonlinear or high dimensional, where the standard Kalman recursion is unstable or infeasible
cards.when_not: the model is linear and low dimensional, where the exact filter is better and cheaper

alternatives.criterion: linear and low dimensional
numerical stability is the issue
high dimensional or nonlinear

output_key_fields: filtered_state, smoothed_state: the state estimates
covariance: state uncertainty, guaranteed positive definite by the square-root form
ensemble_size: draws behind an ensemble filter
loglike: where the filter provides it
interpretation_traps: THE STANDARD KALMAN COVARIANCE RECURSION CAN LOSE POSITIVE DEFINITENESS numerically, which the square-root form prevents by construction -- this is a real failure mode in long or ill-conditioned models
ensemble filters underestimate covariance with small ensembles, which is why inflation and localisation exist
a nonlinear filter's log-likelihood is a simulation estimate and is not directly comparable across ensemble sizes
sources: Evensen 2003 (Ocean Dynamics 53:343-367)
Durbin & Koopman 2012, Time Series Analysis by State Space Methods, 2nd ed.
filterpy
